name: Spaulding Life Sciences Center
use: Biological sciences (COLSA): teaching and research labs, aquatic research core, bioreactor core, natural history collections
architect: Original unknown; 2019–24 addition and renovation by Ellenzweig
style: 1960 brick lab slab spanning College Brook, plus contemporary addition

renovations.what: Partial renovation as part of the Rudman Hall project
Spaulding Biosciences Project: ~47,000 sq ft addition then full renovation of the 83,000 sq ft original; new power, heating and cooling; ribbon cutting June 6, 2025

facts.text: Dedicated May 6, 1960; begun 1958 with state funds and a U.S. Public Health Service grant.
The building spans College Brook, presenting three levels from the ravine and two from DeMeritt Road.
The $95.5 million expansion and renovation is the largest capital project in UNH history; construction wrapped up June 2024.
Ellenzweig designed the addition around "science in action," with a first-floor public gallery along a main pedestrian route.
It now has research neighborhoods, an aquatic research core with freshwater and saltwater labs, a bioreactor core and expanded study areas.
In 2019 planners said the old air system needed replacing; only the large lecture hall and two teaching labs renovated around 2016 were to be kept.

verdict: 1960 lab slab over College Brook, rebuilt and expanded by 2024 in UNH's largest-ever project: new labs, aquatic cores and a public science gallery.
notes: No licensed photo of Spaulding found on Commons or Flickr CC; references only. A/C marked yes from the new heating/cooling systems (TNH 2019) rather than an explicit statement. Cost figures vary: $86M (2019 plan), $89M (Skanska release, not opened), $95.5M (UNH 2025). Addition size 47,000 (UNH) vs 47,500/50,000 elsewhere. LEED Silver target from old row not confirmed. notunh name "Spaulding Life Sciences" is fine; archives index calls it Spaulding Hall.
